title: 5 Simple Ways To Be More Likeable To Your Students students/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin challenges the belief that teachers must be stern and serious to maintain control, arguing instead that likeability is a powerful, largely automatic source of behavioral leverage. He offers five simple, low-effort ways to become more likeable: relaxing and releasing physical tension before students arrive, smiling more often, being authentically oneself rather than hiding personality out of fear of misbehavior, telling short personal or fictional stories, and actively joining in class fun rather than just permitting it. He closes with a "soup" metaphor, arguing that the real management payoff comes from maximizing the contrast between how good it feels to be part of a likeable teacher's class and how unpleasant it feels to be excluded from it via time-out, since that contrast is what gives consequences their bite.
points: Likeability functions as automatic behavioral leverage - students who like their teacher want to please them.
Five simple, low-effort habits build likeability: relaxing, smiling, being authentically oneself, storytelling, and joining in class fun.
Hiding one's personality out of fear of encouraging misbehavior instead stifles charisma and weakens teaching effectiveness.
Actively participating in class fun, rather than merely allowing it, produces a much larger likeability boost.
The wider the contrast between belonging to an enjoyable class and being excluded from it, the more effective consequences like time-out become.
quotes: If your students like you, they'll want to please you and seek your approval. Which gives you leverage-leverage to influence behavior like almost nothing else.
The prevailing wisdom says that teachers need to be grim-faced and serious or students will walk all over them. Hogwash.
A smile is the first step to creating a mutual admiration society with your students; the more you smile at them, the more they’ll smile back.
Keeping your personality under lock and key stifles your charisma, making you appear dry, dull, and humorless—which is the death knell of effective teaching.
Nothing is more effective in creating leverage and admiration than being a good storyteller. Its transformational powers can put your students into the palm of your hand.
Having fun as a class is a potent leverage builder, but if you join your class in the fun, if you take an active part in it, your likeability will skyrocket.
The wider you can make the gap between what it feels like to be part of the class (savory, delicious soup), and being separated from it (bitter, unappetizing soup), the more effective you’ll be.
